failures.claim: Governance arrangements support oversight of climate-related risks and opportunities through Board and committee consideration, management-level committee structures, and integration of climate-related risk management into enterprise risk management (ERM).
The Board is the primary governance body that considers climate-related risks and opportunities through its meeting agenda and discussions.
Across the reported governance records, the Board held 4, 7 and 8 full Board meetings per year.
Across the reported governance records, climate-related matters were included on the Board agenda 69.8% of the time.

Board minutes evidence that Board discussions on climate-related matters include transition plan review, scenario analysis, TCFD review, net zero progress, carbon credit approval, and executive remuneration ESG KPIs.
Climate risk reporting is provided to the Board on a semi-annual basis.
An ESG committee is in place.
Across the reported governance records, the ESG committee met 5, 6 and 7 times per year.
Climate-related considerations are incorporated into decisions on major transactions through a climate check for major transactions.
A portion of executive remuneration is linked to climate-related factors; across the reported governance records, the proportion linked was 8.7%, 15.3% and 15.1%.
Management oversight of climate-related risks and opportunities is delegated to a management-level committee.

Across the reported governance records, the management committee identified for this purpose is recorded as the Group Sustainability Committee, ESG Executive Committee, and Climate Risk Management Committee.
Climate-related risk management is integrated into ERM.
Board climate expertise is tracked; across the reported governance records, 33.5%, 35.5% and 37.5% of the Board was identified as having climate expertise.
A skills development programme is in place.
